question: What is the number of ordered triples \((a, b, c)\) of positive integers, with \(a \le b \le c \le 9,\) such that there exists a (non-degenerate) triangle \(\triangle ABC\) with an integer inradius for which \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are the lengths of the altitudes from \(A\) to \(\overline{BC},\) \(B\) to \(\overline{AC},\) and \(C\) to \(\overline{AB},\) respectively? (Recall that the inradius of a triangle is the radius of the largest possible circle that can be inscribed in the triangle.)
solution:
The sides of a triangle are inversely proportional to their corresponding altitudes. Combining this fact with the triangle inequality will greatly restrict the possible integers.

Let \(K\) be the area, \(r\) the inradius, and \(x=BC\), \(y=CA\), \(z=AB\). The base-height area formula gives
\[
x=\frac{2K}{a},\qquad y=\frac{2K}{b},\qquad z=\frac{2K}{c}.
\]
Joining the incenter to the three vertices divides the triangle into three triangles, each with height \(r\) above its corresponding side. Thus
\[
K=\frac{r(x+y+z)}2
 =rK\left(\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c\right),
\]
so
\[
\frac1r=\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c.
\]
Because all three altitudes are at most \(9\), the right side is at least \(1/3\). Therefore the positive integer \(r\) belongs to \(\{1,2,3\}\).

Since \(a\) is the smallest altitude, \(x\) is the largest side. The strict triangle inequality \(x<y+z\) gives
\[
\frac1a<\frac1b+\frac1c.
\]
Also, \(a\le b\le c\) implies that every reciprocal is at most \(1/a\). Consequently,
\[
\frac2a<\frac1r\le\frac3a,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad 2r<a\le3r.
\]
We now have very few cases.

- If \(r=1\), then \(a=3\). The three reciprocals sum to \(1\) and are each at most \(1/3\), forcing \(a=b=c=3\).
- If \(r=2\), then \(a=5\) or \(6\). When \(a=6\), equality similarly forces \(b=c=6\). When \(a=5\), we need
  \[
  \frac1b+\frac1c=\frac3{10}.
  \]
  Since \(b\le c\), we have \(3/10\le2/b\), so \(5\le b\le6\). For \(b=5\), we get \(c=10>9\); for \(b=6\), we get \(c=15/2\), which is not an integer. Neither works.
- If \(r=3\), the reciprocal sum is \(1/3\). Each term is at least \(1/9\), forcing \(a=b=c=9\).

Each remaining triple is realizable: scale an equilateral triangle to have altitude \(h=3,6,\) or \(9\). The reciprocal formula gives its inradius as \(h/3\), an integer.

The triples are \((3,3,3)\), \((6,6,6)\), and \((9,9,9)\). The answer is \(\boxed{3}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
